stem: In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle PQR\), in a one to one correspondence of vertices, \(\dfrac{AB}{QR} = \dfrac{BC}{PR} = \dfrac{CA}{PQ}\), then ____ statement is true.
solution: **(B)** \(\triangle PQR \sim \triangle CAB\). The equal ratios pair side AB with QR, side BC with RP and side CA with PQ. AB and CA share vertex A, while QR and PQ share vertex Q, so A corresponds to Q. In the same way BC and AB share vertex B, while RP and QR share R, so vertex B corresponds to R, and the remaining vertex C corresponds to P. \(\therefore\) the correspondence is \(ABC \leftrightarrow QRP\), i.e. \(PQR \leftrightarrow CAB\), and by the SSS test \(\triangle PQR \sim \triangle CAB\).
figureNote: p-01: two triangles side by side, a smaller triangle ABC (A top, B bottom left, C bottom right) and a larger triangle PQR (Q top, R bottom left, P bottom right).

stem: Two circles of radii 5.5 cm and 3.3 cm respectively touch each other externally. Then the distance between their centres is ____.
solution: **(B)** 8.8 cm. When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centres is the sum of their radii. \(\therefore\) distance \(= 5.5 + 3.3 = 8.8\) cm. The value 2.2 cm is the difference of the radii, which applies only to circles touching internally.

stem: Seg AB is parallel to Y-axis and co-ordinates of point A are \((1, 3)\), then the co-ordinates of point B are ____.
solution: **(D)** \((1, -3)\). Every point on a line parallel to the Y-axis has the same x co-ordinate. Point A has x co-ordinate 1, so point B must also have x co-ordinate 1. \(\therefore\) B is \((1, -3)\), the only given point whose x co-ordinate is 1.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: The volume of a cube of side 10 cm is ____.
solution: **(A)** 1000 cm\(^3\). Volume of a cube \(= (\text{side})^3\). \(\therefore\) volume \(= 10^3 = 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1000\) cm\(^3\).

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle C = 30^\circ\), \(AC = 12\) cm, then find AB.
solution: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle C = 30^\circ\), so \(\angle A = 60^\circ\) and it is a \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle. By the \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) theorem, the side opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle is half the hypotenuse. \(\therefore AB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 = 6\) cm.
figureNote: p-03: right triangle ABC with the right angle at B (A top, B bottom left, C bottom right), hypotenuse AC marked 12 cm and angle C marked 30 degrees.

stem: In the above figure, \(m(\text{arc } MN) = 70^\circ\), find \(\angle MLN\).
solution: \(\angle MLN\) is inscribed in the circle and intercepts arc MN. By the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of an inscribed angle is half the measure of its intercepted arc. \(\therefore \angle MLN = \dfrac{1}{2} \times m(\text{arc } MN) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 70^\circ = 35^\circ\).
figureNote: p-03: circle with its centre marked by a dot; triangle LMN inscribed in it with L at the top and chord MN at the bottom.

stem: Find the value of \(\sin\theta \times \operatorname{cosec}\theta\).
solution: Since \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\), \(\sin\theta \times \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \sin\theta \times \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\). \(\therefore \sin\theta \times \operatorname{cosec}\theta = 1\).

subtopic: Area of Sector and Segment of a Circle
stem: If radius of a circle is 4 cm and length of an arc is 10 cm, then find the area of the sector.
solution: Area of sector \(= \dfrac{l \times r}{2}\), where \(l\) is the length of the arc and \(r\) the radius. \(\therefore\) area of sector \(= \dfrac{10 \times 4}{2} = 20\) cm\(^2\).

stem: In the above figure, chord PQ and chord RS intersect at point T. Then complete the following activity to prove \(\angle STQ = \dfrac{1}{2}[m(\text{arc } SQ) + m(\text{arc } PR)]\).
solution: \(\angle STQ\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle PTS\). \(\therefore \angle STQ = \angle SPQ + \angle PSR\) (remote interior angles theorem of a triangle). Now \(\angle SPQ = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } SQ)\) and \(\angle PSR = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } PR)\) (inscribed angle theorem). \(\therefore \angle STQ = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } SQ) + \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } PR)\). \(\therefore \angle STQ = \dfrac{1}{2}[m(\text{arc } SQ) + m(\text{arc } PR)]\).
figureNote: p-04: circle with chords PQ and RS intersecting at interior point T; P and S on the upper arc, R on the left, Q at the lower right; segment PS drawn.

stem: If \(\sec\theta = \dfrac{25}{7}\), complete the following activity to find the value of \(\tan\theta\).
solution: We have \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta\). \(\therefore 1 + \tan^2\theta = \left(\dfrac{25}{7}\right)^2 = \dfrac{625}{49}\). \(\therefore \tan^2\theta = \dfrac{625}{49} - 1 = \dfrac{625 - 49}{49} = \dfrac{576}{49}\). \(\therefore \tan\theta = \dfrac{24}{7}\). Check: \(1 + \dfrac{576}{49} = \dfrac{625}{49} = \sec^2\theta\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Complete the following activity to find the volume of a cone if the radius of its base is 7 cm and its perpendicular height is 6 cm.
solution: Here, radius \(r = 7\) cm and height \(h = 6\) cm. Volume of cone \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\) (formula). \(= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times 6 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 49 \times 6 = 22 \times 7 \times 2\). \(\therefore\) volume of cone \(= 308\) cm\(^3\).

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Construct a tangent to a circle with centre P and radius 3.2 cm at any point M on it.
solution: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at its point of contact, so the tangent at M is the line through M perpendicular to radius PM. Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle with centre P and radius 3.2 cm. (2) Take any point M on the circle and draw ray PM. (3) Draw line \(l\) through M perpendicular to ray PM. Line \(l\) is the required tangent to the circle at point M.

stem: In \(\triangle PQR\), seg RS bisects \(\angle PRQ\). If \(PR = 15\), \(RQ = 20\), \(PS = 12\), then find SQ.
solution: In \(\triangle PQR\), seg RS bisects \(\angle PRQ\). By the property of an angle bisector of a triangle, \(\dfrac{PR}{RQ} = \dfrac{PS}{SQ}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{15}{20} = \dfrac{12}{SQ}\). \(\therefore SQ = \dfrac{12 \times 20}{15} = 16\). Check: \(\dfrac{12}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{15}{20}\).
figureNote: p-06: triangle PQR (R at the top right, P at the left, Q at the bottom) with seg RS bisecting angle PRQ, S on side PQ; the two equal angles at R are marked.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Find the surface area of a sphere of diameter 14 cm.
solution: Radius \(r = \dfrac{14}{2} = 7\) cm. Surface area of a sphere \(= 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 4 \times 22 \times 7\). \(\therefore\) surface area of the sphere \(= 616\) cm\(^2\).

stem: In the above figure, \(\angle PQR = 90^\circ\), seg \(QN \perp\) seg PR, \(PN = 9\), \(NR = 16\), find QN.
solution: In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle PQR = 90^\circ\) and seg \(QN \perp\) hypotenuse PR. By the theorem of geometric mean, \(QN^2 = PN \times NR\). \(\therefore QN^2 = 9 \times 16 = 144\). \(\therefore QN = 12\).
figureNote: p-07: right triangle PQR with the right angle at Q (P top left, Q bottom left, R bottom right); seg QN perpendicular to hypotenuse PR, with PN = 9 and NR = 16 marked.

stem: Find the slope of the line passing through the points \(A(3, 3)\) and \(B(5, 7)\).
solution: Slope \(= \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\). \(\therefore\) slope of line AB \(= \dfrac{7 - 3}{5 - 3} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\).

stem: In the given figure, \(AB \parallel CD \parallel EF\). If \(AC = 12\), \(CE = 9\), \(BD = 8\), then complete the following activity to find DF.
solution: \(AB \parallel CD \parallel EF\). \(\therefore \dfrac{AC}{CE} = \dfrac{BD}{DF}\) (property of three parallel lines and their transversals). \(\therefore \dfrac{12}{9} = \dfrac{8}{DF}\). \(\therefore DF = \dfrac{8 \times 9}{12}\). \(\therefore DF = 6\). Check: \(\dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{12}{9}\).
figureNote: p-07: three parallel horizontal lines AB, CD, EF cut by two transversals; points A, C, E lie on the left transversal and B, D, F on the right transversal (the question text continues on p-08).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: A cylinder is having radius 7 cm and height 21 cm. Complete the following activity to calculate its volume and circumference of its base.
solution: Radius \(r = 7\) cm, height \(h = 21\) cm. Volume of cylinder \(= \pi r^2 h\) (formula) \(= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 21 = 154 \times 21\). \(\therefore\) volume of cylinder \(= 3234\) cm\(^3\). Circumference of base \(= 2\pi r\) (formula) \(= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7\). \(\therefore\) circumference of base \(= 44\) cm.

stem: Prove that, 'Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary'.
solution: Given: \(\square ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. To prove: \(\angle B + \angle D = 180^\circ\) and \(\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ\). Proof: Arc ABC is intercepted by inscribed \(\angle ADC\), and arc ADC is intercepted by inscribed \(\angle ABC\). \(\therefore \angle ADC = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } ABC)\) ...(I) and \(\angle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } ADC)\) ...(II) (inscribed angle theorem). Adding (I) and (II), \(\angle ADC + \angle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}[m(\text{arc } ABC) + m(\text{arc } ADC)]\). Arcs ABC and ADC together make the whole circle, so \(m(\text{arc } ABC) + m(\text{arc } ADC) = 360^\circ\). \(\therefore \angle B + \angle D = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 360^\circ = 180^\circ\). The sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is \(360^\circ\), \(\therefore \angle A + \angle C = 360^\circ - 180^\circ = 180^\circ\). Hence the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle with centre P and radius 3.5 cm. Take point Q at a distance 8 cm from the centre. Construct tangents to the circle from point Q.
solution: A tangent from Q touches the circle at a point A where \(\angle PAQ = 90^\circ\), so A lies on the circle with diameter PQ (angle in a semicircle). Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle with centre P and radius 3.5 cm. (2) Take point Q such that \(PQ = 8\) cm and draw seg PQ. (3) Draw the perpendicular bisector of seg PQ; let it meet PQ at M, so \(PM = MQ = 4\) cm. (4) With centre M and radius MP (4 cm), draw a circle cutting the given circle at points A and B. (5) Draw lines QA and QB. Lines QA and QB are the required tangents. Check: each tangent segment measures \(\sqrt{8^2 - 3.5^2} = \sqrt{51.75}\), about 7.2 cm.

stem: Show that points \(P(-2, 3)\), \(Q(1, 2)\), \(R(4, 1)\) are collinear.
solution: Slope of line PQ \(= \dfrac{2 - 3}{1 - (-2)} = \dfrac{-1}{3}\). Slope of line QR \(= \dfrac{1 - 2}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{-1}{3}\). \(\therefore\) slope of PQ \(=\) slope of QR, and point Q is common to both lines. \(\therefore\) points P, Q and R are collinear.

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
stem: If \(\triangle PQR \sim \triangle LMN\), \(9 \times A(\triangle PQR) = 16 \times A(\triangle LMN)\) and \(QR = 20\), then find MN.
solution: \(9 \times A(\triangle PQR) = 16 \times A(\triangle LMN)\), \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle PQR)}{A(\triangle LMN)} = \dfrac{16}{9}\). Since \(\triangle PQR \sim \triangle LMN\), by the theorem of areas of similar triangles, \(\dfrac{A(\triangle PQR)}{A(\triangle LMN)} = \dfrac{QR^2}{MN^2}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{QR^2}{MN^2} = \dfrac{16}{9}\), so \(\dfrac{QR}{MN} = \dfrac{4}{3}\) (taking square roots). \(\therefore \dfrac{20}{MN} = \dfrac{4}{3}\). \(\therefore MN = \dfrac{20 \times 3}{4} = 15\). Check: \(\dfrac{20^2}{15^2} = \dfrac{400}{225} = \dfrac{16}{9}\).

stem: \(\triangle ABC\) is an equilateral triangle. Point D is on seg BC such that \(BD = \dfrac{1}{5} BC\). Then prove that \(\dfrac{AD^2}{AB^2} = \dfrac{21}{25}\).
solution: Given: \(\triangle ABC\) is equilateral, D lies on seg BC and \(BD = \dfrac{1}{5}BC\). To prove: \(\dfrac{AD^2}{AB^2} = \dfrac{21}{25}\). Construction: Draw seg \(AM \perp\) side BC, with M on BC. Proof: Let \(AB = BC = AC = a\). In an equilateral triangle the perpendicular from a vertex bisects the opposite side, so \(BM = \dfrac{a}{2}\). \(BD = \dfrac{a}{5}\), \(\therefore DM = BM - BD = \dfrac{a}{2} - \dfrac{a}{5} = \dfrac{3a}{10}\). In right \(\triangle AMB\), by Pythagoras theorem, \(AM^2 = AB^2 - BM^2 = a^2 - \dfrac{a^2}{4} = \dfrac{3a^2}{4}\). In right \(\triangle AMD\), by Pythagoras theorem, \(AD^2 = AM^2 + DM^2 = \dfrac{3a^2}{4} + \dfrac{9a^2}{100} = \dfrac{75a^2 + 9a^2}{100} = \dfrac{84a^2}{100} = \dfrac{21a^2}{25}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{AD^2}{AB^2} = \dfrac{21a^2}{25} \div a^2 = \dfrac{21}{25}\).

stem: \(\triangle LMN \sim \triangle LQP\). In \(\triangle LMN\), \(LM = 3.6\) cm, \(\angle L = 50^\circ\), \(LN = 4.2\) cm and \(\dfrac{LM}{LQ} = \dfrac{4}{7}\). Construct \(\triangle LQP\).
solution: Rough work: \(\triangle LMN \sim \triangle LQP\), so L corresponds to L, M to Q and N to P, and \(\dfrac{LM}{LQ} = \dfrac{LN}{LP} = \dfrac{4}{7}\). \(\therefore LQ = \dfrac{7}{4} \times 3.6 = 6.3\) cm and \(LP = \dfrac{7}{4} \times 4.2 = 7.35\) cm, with \(\angle QLP = \angle MLN = 50^\circ\). Steps of construction: (1) Draw seg \(LM = 3.6\) cm, draw ray LX making \(\angle L = 50^\circ\) at L, and mark N on it with \(LN = 4.2\) cm; join MN to complete \(\triangle LMN\). (2) Draw ray LY making an acute angle with ray LM, on the side opposite to N. (3) On ray LY mark seven points \(L_1, L_2, \ldots, L_7\) at equal distances. (4) Join \(L_4M\). (5) Through \(L_7\) draw a line parallel to \(L_4M\), meeting ray LM extended at Q. (6) Through Q draw a line parallel to side MN, meeting ray LN extended at P. \(\triangle LQP\) is the required triangle, with \(LQ = 6.3\) cm and \(LP = 7.35\) cm.

stem: To find the width of the river, a man observes the top of a tree, on the opposite bank making an angle of elevation of \(60^\circ\). When he moves 24 meter backward from bank and observes the same top of the tree, his line of vision makes an angle of elevation of \(30^\circ\). Find the height of the tree and width of the river. \((\sqrt{3} = 1.73)\)
solution: Let AB be the tree, with B its foot on the opposite bank, let C be the man's first position on the bank and D his position after moving 24 m back. Let the width of the river \(BC = x\) m and the height of the tree \(AB = h\) m. In right \(\triangle ABC\), \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BC}\), \(\therefore \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{h}{x}\), \(\therefore h = \sqrt{3}\,x\) ...(I). In right \(\triangle ABD\), \(BD = x + 24\) and \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BD}\), \(\therefore \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h}{x + 24}\), \(\therefore x + 24 = \sqrt{3}\,h\) ...(II). Substituting (I) in (II), \(x + 24 = \sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}\,x = 3x\), \(\therefore 2x = 24\), \(\therefore x = 12\). From (I), \(h = 12\sqrt{3} = 12 \times 1.73 = 20.76\). \(\therefore\) the height of the tree is 20.76 m and the width of the river is 12 m. Check: \(\dfrac{12\sqrt{3}}{36} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan 30^\circ\).

stem: The diameter of circular garden is 13 meter. The distance between two gates of garden is 13 meter. An electric pole is to be erected on the circumference of the garden such that the difference between distance of the pole from each gate is 7 meter. Can such pole be erected? If yes, find the distance of the pole from each gate.
solution: Let A and B be the gates and P the pole on the circumference. The distance between the gates equals the diameter (13 m), so seg AB is a diameter of the garden. \(\angle APB\) is inscribed in a semicircle, \(\therefore \angle APB = 90^\circ\). Let the distance of the pole from the nearer gate be \(x\) m; then its distance from the other gate is \((x + 7)\) m. In right \(\triangle APB\), by Pythagoras theorem, \(x^2 + (x + 7)^2 = 13^2\). \(\therefore x^2 + x^2 + 14x + 49 = 169\), \(\therefore 2x^2 + 14x - 120 = 0\), \(\therefore x^2 + 7x - 60 = 0\), \(\therefore (x + 12)(x - 5) = 0\). A distance cannot be negative, so \(x \ne -12\), and \(x = 5\). \(\therefore\) yes, such a pole can be erected: it is 5 m from one gate and 12 m from the other. Check: \(5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13^2\) and \(12 - 5 = 7\).

stem: The line \(x - 6y + 11 = 0\) bisects the segment joining the points \((8, -1)\) and \((0, k)\), then find the value of \(k\).
solution: The line bisects the segment, so it passes through the midpoint of the segment. By the midpoint formula, the midpoint of the segment joining \((8, -1)\) and \((0, k)\) is \(\left(\dfrac{8 + 0}{2}, \dfrac{-1 + k}{2}\right) = \left(4, \dfrac{k - 1}{2}\right)\). This point lies on \(x - 6y + 11 = 0\): \(4 - 6 \times \dfrac{k - 1}{2} + 11 = 0\), \(\therefore 15 - 3(k - 1) = 0\), \(\therefore k - 1 = 5\). \(\therefore k = 6\). Check: the midpoint is \(\left(4, \dfrac{5}{2}\right)\) and \(4 - 6 \times \dfrac{5}{2} + 11 = 4 - 15 + 11 = 0\).
